title: What European contact meant for the Indigenous Americas
examples: What happened to Native Americans after 1492?
Why did so many Indigenous people die?
How did the Spanish conquer the Aztecs and Inca?

explain.say: Think about meeting people from a land you never knew existed. In 1492, when Columbus's ships reached the Caribbean, two worlds met that had been apart for thousands of years. For the people already living in the Americas, it changed everything. Let's follow what happened.

explain.say: Look at the germ. Europeans brought diseases like smallpox and measles. People in the Americas had never met them, so they had no immunity, which means the body's natural protection. In some places around 90 percent of people died. Why do new germs spread so fast?

explain.say: Now the fire. Spanish soldiers, helped by Indigenous allies and by disease, took the Aztec capital in 1521 and captured the Inca ruler in 1532. Within a few decades, two great empires had fallen. Why do you think allies mattered so much?

faq.a: Christopher Columbus, sailing for Spain, reached islands in the Caribbean, where the Taino people lived. It began lasting contact between Europe and the Americas.

faq.q: Why did so many Indigenous people die from disease?
faq.a: Diseases like smallpox, measles and influenza were new to the Americas, so people had no immunity. Epidemics often spread ahead of the Europeans themselves. Estimates vary, but many regions lost most of their people.
asks: Why did smallpox kill so many?

faq.q: How did small Spanish forces defeat big empires?
faq.a: They had steel weapons, horses and guns, but most important were thousands of Indigenous allies who opposed Aztec or Inca rule, and epidemics that had already weakened the empires.
A Spanish system that gave colonists the right to demand labour and tribute from Indigenous people in an area. In practice it often meant forced labour and abuse.
asks: What was forced labour in New Spain?

faq.q: Do Indigenous peoples still live in the Americas?
faq.a: Yes. Tens of millions of Indigenous people live across the Americas today, speaking hundreds of languages, from Quechua and Guarani in South America to Navajo and Cree in North America.

facts: Columbus first landed in the Bahamas in October 1492.
Bartolome de las Casas wrote against the treatment of Indigenous people in the 1540s and 1550s.
Maize was first domesticated in southern Mexico about 9,000 years ago.

quiz.say: Why did diseases like smallpox kill so many people in the Americas?

options.show: People had no immunity to it
options.say: People had no immunity to it

quiz.why: The diseases were new, so bodies had no built-up protection.

wrong.1: Weather was not the cause; the germs were new.
wrong.2: Hunger was not the main cause; new diseases were.

quiz.say: Who helped the Spanish defeat the Aztecs?
quiz.why: Peoples like the Tlaxcalans, who opposed Aztec rule, fought alongside the Spanish.

wrong.1: The Inca lived far away in the Andes and were conquered later.
